title: introduce-tf-module-gpu-nodepool-identity-wrapper-and-subnet-resolver
author: Samira Patel
description: Motivation: private deployments frequently require tenant-scoped GPU nodepools where the node identity and subnet selection are decoupled from the monolithic installer TF modules. This PR introduces two small, composable Terraform modules: (1) gpu_nodepool_identity_wrapper — a lightweight IAM/instance-profile wrapper that centralizes nodepool identity configuration (assume-role for workload operator, instance profile creation, and optional KMS encryption bindings), and (2) subnet_resolver — a deterministic subnet selection helper that locates matching subnets by tags, AZ affinity, and available IP capacity. Both are aimed at reducing per-tenant duplication in tfstate and making upgrades/rollbacks safer by confining state to narrower keys. Changes: - New module modules/gpu_nodepool_identity/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,README.md} - New module modules/subnet_resolver/{main.tf,variables.tf,README.md} - Installer integration in modules/tenant-gpu-cluster/main.tf (adds optional identity_wrapper and subnet_resolver usage behind feature flags) - Migration helper script scripts/tfstate-prefix-transformer.sh to optionally copy and remap old tfstate keys for tenant-scoped submodules - Acceptance tests added under test/terraform/acceptance/gpu_identity_resolver/ that run plan/apply in a metal-mock env Checklist: - [x] Add module code and README - [x] Add unit/type checks (tflint + fmt) - [x] Add acceptance job to CI pipeline - [x] Confirm no default change in existing installs (feature flags off) - [x] Provide migration instructions and rollback plan Testing performed: - Local tflint/tfsec passes with updated config - Dry-run on staging-backed state bucket using tfstate-prefix-transformer to remap one tenant (linear ENG-4912) - Acceptance suite run in CI using mocked cloud provider (network tag matching tests, identity assume-role tests) - Manual smoke: created tenant cluster with new wrapper and launched sample GPU job to confirm node credentials and NVidia driver init Migration notes: The new modules are opt-in behind variable flags (enable_gpu_identity_wrapper, enable_subnet_resolver default false). For customers who want to migrate state into tenant-scoped tfstate prefixes we provide scripts/tfstate-prefix-transformer.sh with usage examples. Steps: 1) validate current tfstate in staging (backup bucket snapshot) 2) run transformer with --source-key=<old-module> --dest-prefix=tenant/<tenant-id>/ 3) run terraform plan with enable flags enabled and confirm plan only touches intended resources Rollback: If migration produces unexpected drift, run transformer with --reverse to restore original keys and re-run plan with flags disabled Compatibility: preserves current variable schema for tenant-gpu-cluster; new optional vars are backwards compatible. Security: the identity wrapper exposes a minimal assume-role policy and rotates role name if a name collision is detected. KMS bindings are optional and gated by enable_kms_binding var Related work: references to earlier tfstate-shard and lease work (see ENG-4978 and SUP-1248). This PR purposely avoids changing global tfstate layout; it provides a migration path and a safe opt-in toggle for customer operators.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-03-01 after all reviewers approved. Changelog entries aggregated into private-installer v2026.03.1
release_notes:
- Added gpu_nodepool_identity module: centralizes per-tenant node identity (IAM role + instance profile) and optional KMS bindings.
- Added subnet_resolver module: deterministic subnet selection by tags, AZ affinity, and IP capacity heuristics.
- Added tfstate-prefix-transformer helper script for controlled migration of resource keys into tenant-scoped prefixes.
Notes: modules are opt-in behind enable_gpu_identity_wrapper and enable_subnet_resolver. No behavior change unless enabled.
notes_for_ops: Operational guidance: - Before enabling, snapshot tfstate and run transformer in dry-run mode. - For large installations prefer staged migrations (one tenant at a time). - If you use custom IAM role naming, set identity_role_name explicitly to avoid suffixing. - To rollback: run transformer --reverse and disable enable flags, then re-plan.
risk_assessment: low-medium: new modules are opt-in. The primary risk is during migration of tfstate keys; mitigated by transformer dry-run and staged strategy.
qa_acceptance: Acceptance tests cover: tag-matching subnet selection, AZ affinity fallback, assume-role chain for node bootstrap, instance-profile creation. All tests green in CI after fixes.
